notes.summary: An antonym is a word with the opposite meaning (generous and stingy). SSC asks 1 to 2 antonym questions in Tier 1 and more in Tier 2. Most give a single word; the rest underline a word in a sentence, ask you to fill a blank with the opposite of a bracketed word, or ask you to find the opposite among the words of the sentence. The commonest trap is that a synonym of the word is always among the options.

concepts.title: How SSC asks antonym questions
concepts.body:
• Given word: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. ASCENT.
  • Word in a sentence: We lived a very frugal life. The opposite must fit the sentence too (extravagant).
  • Bracket and blank: Sheila ______ (failed) all her classes. Answer: passed, in the same tense.
  • From the sentence: the options are words picked from the sentence; find the one opposite to the named word.

concepts.title: A four-step method
concepts.body:
1. Fix the meaning of the given word (in the sentence, if there is one).
  2. Cross out synonyms. Usually one or two options mean the same thing. Liberty: cross out freedom and autonomy.
  3. Find the exact opposite, same part of speech: ascent (noun) ↔ descent (noun).
  4. Prefer the closest opposite, not just any negative word. Malice (wish to harm) ↔ goodwill, not truth.

concepts.title: Opposites formed with prefixes
concepts.body:
PrefixExamples
un-certain ↔ uncertain, usual ↔ unusual, able ↔ unable
in- / im- / il- / ir-active ↔ inactive, mature ↔ immature, legal ↔ illegal, relevant ↔ irrelevant
dis-honest ↔ dishonest, agree ↔ disagree, approve ↔ disapprove
mis-trust ↔ mistrust, fortune ↔ misfortune
non-violent ↔ non-violent, essential ↔ non-essential
-ful ↔ -lesscareful ↔ careless, hopeful ↔ hopeless
pro- ↔ anti- / con-pros ↔ cons, prologue ↔ epilogue
in- ↔ ex-include ↔ exclude, import ↔ export, internal ↔ external
Watch the exceptions: flammable and inflammable mean the same (easily burnt); valuable and invaluable are not opposites (invaluable = priceless).

concepts.title: Look-alike traps
concepts.body:
Some options are placed only because they look like the answer.
  • Ascent ↔ descent (going down), not decent (proper) or dissent (disagreement).
  • Affluent ↔ indigent (poor), not fluent or influential.
  • Eminent (famous) ↔ unknown, obscure; imminent means about to happen.
  • Moral ↔ immoral; amoral means without any sense of morals, a different idea.
  • Uninterested (not interested) is not the same as disinterested (impartial).

varieties.name: Antonym of a given word
varieties.how: Find the meaning, cross out the synonyms in the options, then pick the closest opposite of the same part of speech.

example.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
Liberty
steps: Options: slavery, freedom, autonomy, reservation. Freedom and autonomy are synonyms; cross them out.
Reservation is unrelated. The opposite of freedom is slavery.

varieties.name: Antonym of a word in a sentence
varieties.how: Work out the meaning of the marked word in this sentence, then choose the opposite that would also fit the sentence.

example.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word.
We lived a very frugal life during our childhood.
steps: The opposite of spending little is spending too much: extravagant.

varieties.name: Fill the blank with an antonym
varieties.how: Take the opposite of the bracketed word and keep its form (tense, number, part of speech) so it fits the blank.

example.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.
Sheila ______ (failed) all her classes.
steps: Options: passed, flunked, resized, flopped. Flunked and flopped are synonyms of failed.

varieties.name: Find the antonym inside the sentence
varieties.how: Read the sentence for the word that means the opposite of the named word. Ignore words that are merely nearby or related.

example.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the word unsure from the given sentence.
Himanshi is preparing customised gifts for Mehul's retirement, but she is certain the date will not change.
steps: Options from the sentence: date, certain, customised, gifts.
Only certain means the opposite of doubtful.

tips: Cross out synonyms first; most questions have at least one.
Keep the part of speech: ascent (noun) needs descent (noun).
Choose the nearest opposite, not a word that is merely negative.
In a sentence, the meaning can change: light bag ↔ heavy, light room ↔ dark.
Use prefixes as clues (un-, in-, dis-, mis-), but check exceptions like inflammable.
In bracket-blank questions, the answer keeps the tense of the bracketed word.
traps: A synonym is placed in the options to catch hurried readers.
Flammable and inflammable are not opposites; both mean easily burnt.
Amoral is not the antonym of moral; immoral is.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
Generous
questions.solution: Generous = willing to give. Opposite = unwilling to spend or give = Stingy. Liberal and Kind are near-synonyms.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
Expand

Select the most appropriate antonym of the bold word.
His speech was so verbose that half the audience fell asleep.
questions.solution: Verbose = using more words than needed. Opposite = Concise (brief and clear). Wordy is the synonym trap.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
Affluent
questions.solution: Affluent = rich. Opposite = Indigent (very poor). Fluent is a look-alike trap.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the bold word.
The manager gave a tacit approval to the plan by simply nodding.
questions.solution: Tacit = understood without being stated. Opposite = Explicit (stated clearly). Silent and Implied are synonyms.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
Ameliorate
questions.solution: Ameliorate = make a bad situation better. Opposite = Aggravate (make worse). Improve, Alleviate, Amend are all close in meaning to ameliorate.
